question: Can optimizing the trajectory of a finite-radius ball tangent to the graph of a loss provide a useful non-local, scale-selective alternative to pointwise gradient methods?

key_findings.claim: RBO replaces descent on f with motion constrained to the upper offset surface traced by centers of radius-rho balls tangent to the loss graph.
key_findings.evidence: Each update takes a tangent step for the ball center and solves a projection/tangency subproblem back to the invariant distance d(c,Gamma)=rho. The parameter returned to the network is the current contact point.

key_findings.claim: The proven 'ironing' result is limited: strong smoothing is established for bounded continuous functions as radius grows, while ordinary unbounded neural losses receive only weaker geometric statements.
key_findings.evidence: The main theorem's local-uniform convergence assumes a bounded graph. The paper acknowledges common losses are unbounded, then proves monotonic reachability and that local minima sharper than inverse radius are unreachable under C2 smoothness.

key_findings.claim: In short 10-epoch image experiments, RBO has the highest accuracy in every reported row but often much worse validation cross-entropy than SAM.
key_findings.evidence: Over five runs, RBO versus SAM accuracy is 71.58 versus 69.09 on CIFAR-10/ResNet-8 and 50.07 versus 47.17 on CIFAR-100/VGG-9, but loss is 1.538 versus 0.885 and 2.836 versus 1.986. The fixed hyperparameters and unusually short training favor rapid optimization rather than final tuned performance.

key_findings.claim: The method's computational feasibility and scaling are unresolved.
key_findings.evidence: Every update embeds an approximate optimization/projection solver; the paper flags significantly greater cost, accumulated solver error, chaotic large-radius dynamics, and a possible curse of dimensionality. Tests use small networks on one RTX 4050.

method.core_idea: Use a geometrically non-local optimizer whose finite radius determines which loss-surface features are reachable and therefore smooths small-scale wrinkles.
method.mechanism: Maintain a ball center at fixed distance from the loss graph, move along the local tangent direction, numerically solve for a new contact point satisfying tangency, and update model parameters to that contact point.
assumptions: Euclidean geometry in raw parameter coordinates is meaningful for loss-landscape scale.
The tangency/contact subproblem can be solved accurately and cheaply in high dimensions.
Suppressing features smaller than rho improves generalization rather than deleting useful narrow basins.
A single radius and unusually large learning rate transfer across models and datasets.

techniques.role: Defines a non-local smoothed geometry through finite-radius tangency.
Numerically restores the invariant after a tangent center step.
Relates radius to which minima can be contacted.
Explores stability across interaction scale and step size.

evaluations.setting: MNIST with MLP, ResNet-6, VGG-9 and CIFAR-10/100 with ResNet-8 and VGG-9 for 10 epochs.
evaluations.metric: Best validation loss and accuracy over five runs with 95% confidence intervals.
evaluations.result: RBO has the best accuracy in all seven rows and very rapid training, while SAM has lower loss in most rows.
evaluations.baseline: SGD, Entropy-SGD, and SAM using one recommended hyperparameter setting each rather than equal tuning budgets.

evaluations.setting: MNIST MLP radius/learning-rate sweep for three epochs.
evaluations.result: Accuracy rises over much of the tested range and remains stable at learning rates up to 100, but radius 30 with rate 100 diverges.
evaluations.baseline: No comparable sweep or best-of-budget selection is reported for baselines.

limitations: The strongest ironing theorem excludes typical unbounded neural-network losses.
Raw-parameter sharpness and Euclidean radii change under function-preserving reparameterization.
The inner contact solver adds unspecified per-step compute and approximation error.
Comparisons last only 10 epochs on small image models and do not include modern AdamW-scale workloads.
RBO receives a radius/rate exploration while baselines use single recommended settings.
Higher classification accuracy paired with worse cross-entropy is not analyzed for calibration or robustness.
No wall-clock, FLOP, memory, or solver-iteration table supports efficiency claims.
failure_modes: A large radius can skip a narrow but well-generalizing basin or make the projection ill-conditioned.
Contact-point non-uniqueness can cause discontinuous or chaotic updates.
Approximate projection errors can accumulate and violate the geometric invariant.
Parameter rescaling can change reachability without changing the represented function.
reusable_insights: Optimizer neighborhoods should be interpreted as an explicit scale parameter and audited for reparameterization sensitivity.
Non-local optimizer comparisons require equal hyperparameter-search and wall-clock budgets.
Accuracy, cross-entropy, calibration, sharpness, and robustness should all be reported when smoothing changes confidence.
Projection residuals and invariant drift are essential diagnostics for geometry-constrained updates.
open_questions: Can RBO be approximated with one or two Hessian-vector products rather than an inner solver?
Is there a function-space or normalized metric that makes radius invariant to parameter scaling?
Does RBO retain gains after full schedules and tuned SAM/AdamW on ImageNet or Transformers?
How do dimension and curvature control contact uniqueness and solver error?

competitive_landscape.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Efficiently Improving Generalization
competitive_landscape.difference: SAM minimizes worst loss in a parameter neighborhood with a cheap adversarial approximation; RBO follows an offset-surface contact geometry that uses more neighborhood shape but requires an inner projection solve.

competitive_landscape.title: Entropy-SGD: Biasing Gradient Descent Into Wide Valleys
competitive_landscape.difference: Entropy-SGD optimizes a local-entropy-smoothed loss via Langevin inner loops; RBO uses deterministic ball reachability and contact geometry but shares substantial computational overhead.

competitive_landscape.title: SmoothOut: Smoothing Out Sharp Minima to Improve Generalization in Deep Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: SmoothOut averages uniformly perturbed network copies and supplies a stochastic approximation; RBO smooths through a geometric envelope whose practical solver cost and invariance are less established.

novelty_assessment: The rolling-contact geometric formulation and reachability results are genuinely distinctive. Its practical advantage over established neighborhood smoothing is preliminary because the main theorem has bounded-loss scope, the metric is parameterization dependent, and experiments do not match tuning or computational budgets.
reviewer_notes: Read all 14 pages, including update geometry, proofs, complete Table 1, radius sweep, and acknowledged scaling/solver issues. SAM, Entropy-SGD, and SmoothOut primary records were checked on 2026-08-23.
